record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study examines scaling in image diffusion models and reports how training loss and image-generation quality vary with model scale, extending the scaling question to another modality.
record.gate_note: The study does not measure held-out language-model cross-entropy, fit power laws, test extrapolation from small language-model runs, or find a compute-optimal parameter/token split. It reports image-diffusion training loss and FID results; FID values are recorded as related findings, not as language-model downstream-task results.
record.test_reason: Image latent-diffusion transformers on ImageNet are a new setting. Appendix C (Fig. 13) reports training loss across model sizes and patch sizes, which bears on V5. The paper fits no power law, so its results show only the direction of the scale effect, not the power-law form V5 names.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that higher-Gflops DiTs consistently get lower FID and lower training loss, and that DiTs 'inherit the excellent scaling properties' of transformers. They say the loss trend is consistent with language-model scaling, but fit no power law. They also report state-of-the-art FID: 2.27 at 256×256 and 3.04 at 512×512.
record.recipe_differences: Image diffusion transformers are evaluated using training loss and image-generation metrics, rather than language-model held-out cross-entropy, token/compute allocation, or power-law extrapolation.
record.method_sensitivity: Image-generation FID differs with model size and patch size; the authors also report that model Gflops and patch size affect compute efficiency.

fits_no_version.finding: FID-50K at 400K steps is strongly correlated with transformer Gflops (correlation −0.93, Fig. 8). Configs with similar Gflops get similar FID (e.g. S/2 at 68.40 vs B/4 at 68.38), so parameter count alone does not determine quality.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In image diffusion transformers, forward-pass compute (Gflops), not parameter count, predicts sample quality.

fits_no_version.finding: Plotted against total training compute, small DiT models become compute-inefficient relative to larger models trained for fewer steps (Fig. 9); XL/2 overtakes XL/4 after about 10^10 Gflops.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For a fixed training compute budget in image diffusion, larger and higher-Gflop models give better FID.

fits_no_version.finding: Extra sampling compute does not close the gap for smaller models (Fig. 10): XL/2 at 128 steps reaches FID-10K 23.7, versus 25.9 for L/2 at 1000 steps, while using 5× less sampling compute.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Test-time sampling compute cannot substitute for model compute in diffusion transformers.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision
record.problems: The training-loss evidence is plotted without a reported power-law fit or held-out loss measurement. FID is an image-generation metric, not the language-model held-out loss in the claim. The text reports correlations and trends, not uncertainty estimates for these findings.
record.rows_left_out: None of the reported results meeting the row criteria were omitted.

untested.parts: A fitted power-law form for image-diffusion loss; held-out loss; scaling in data or tokens trained on; video, repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer.
Extrapolation from small runs; not studied.
Compute-optimal parameter/token split; not studied (Fig. 9 is an FID-vs-compute analogue in images).
Dependence of exponents on fitting choices; no fits are made.

FID as a function of total training compute (compute efficiency)

record.verdict_notes: No verdict label is given. The only row linked to V5 (R1) shows loss falling with scale, but with no power-law fit, no held-out loss and no exponent, so it cannot show the power-law form V5 names. Researchers may read it as directional evidence consistent with V5 at most. All FID rows are unlinked image-quality metrics.

conditions.value: model Gflops increased via transformer size or number of input tokens

rows.measure: Training loss (noise-prediction mean-squared error plus DKL)
rows.value: Scaled-up DiT models exhibit lower training losses; increasing Gflops makes loss decrease more rapidly and saturate at a lower value.
rows.note: The text states this trend, while the plotted curves do not provide a fitted power-law form or held-out loss measurement.
rows.check: The measure is training loss (MSE plus KL), not held-out loss, and no power-law fit or exponent is reported. The curves show loss falls with Gflops but cannot show whether the form is a power law. The subject should be the 12 DiT configs at 256×256 plus the XL/2 models; the 512×512 curve is only XL/2.
